findings.message: The doctor and dispatch apply different rules for when `node_label` is required alongside `bundle_claim`. `check_bundles` accepts `bundle_claim` without `node_label` on a cluster with at most one node (`[[ -n "${FLEET_NODE_LABEL:-}" ]] || (( n <= 1 ))`). `parse_pod_inputs` in lib/podspec.sh always dies when `bundle_claim` is set without `node_label`, and the README says node_label is required. ac16 pins the doctor's version: a single-node run without a label asserts `ok bundles: fleet-bundles`. Fix: make the doctor report `missing bundles: ... set fleet.node_label` whenever the claim is set and the label is not, matching dispatch. Better still, call one shared predicate from both places.
findings.scenario: Single-node k3s, `fleet.bundle_claim: fleet-bundles`, no `fleet.node_label`, claim applied → `specclaw-fleet doctor` prints `ok bundles: fleet-bundles` and `all checks ok`, but every `specclaw-fleet dispatch` dies with `fleet.bundle_claim is set but fleet.node_label is not`.

findings.message: The bundles check makes sure `node_label` matches exactly one node, but not that this node is the one the claim is bound to. It already reads the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation, yet only uses it to tell the Pending states apart. A Bound claim on node A with the label on node B passes. Fix: when the claim has a selected node, compare it to the single labelled node and report `missing bundles: claim lives on <A>, node_label matches <B>`.
findings.scenario: The first Job runs before the operator labels a node, so the local-path claim binds to node-a. The operator then labels node-b with `specclaw.fleet/worker=true` → doctor prints `ok bundles: fleet-bundles`, but every Job is pinned to node-b and its volume can only attach on node-a, so pods stay Pending until the Job deadline.

findings.message: Each push attempt runs `git push` with no timeout, and the retry loop now runs up to 9 of them. It also adds 65 s of default pauses and a full `repack -a -d -f`, all after the agent deadline has already been used (`deliver` ignores TERM). A stalled push is never cut off, so the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds kills the pod before `record ... exit=push-failed` or `save_bundle` runs. Fix: bound each attempt (for example `timeout <s> git push` or `-c http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime`) and cap the whole retry budget to fit inside the Job's post-agent margin.
findings.scenario: The agent hits the deadline and `deliver deadline` starts. The remote accepts the TCP connection but stalls the pack upload → the first `git push` never returns → the Job deadline kills the pod. No push-failed record, no `bundle=saved`, the work item is left in its running state, and `--retry` has no bundle to resume from.

findings.message: `bundle=none` is recorded both when `bundle_claim` is off (no /fleet/bundles folder) and when a configured save failed. The README documents `bundle=none` as "when it could not". Record `bundle=off` (or omit the field) when no bundle folder is configured, so a real save failure is distinguishable.

The new test cases ac40_push_retry.sh, ac41_bundles.sh and ac42_bundles_real_git.sh are added with mode 100644, while sibling cases such as ac14_dispatch_inputs.sh are 100755. If the runner executes cases directly, these will not run. `chmod +x` them for consistency.
